subtitle: Lesson 10 · Quantum Error Correction Basics

eyebrow: Encoding: spreading one qubit across three

steps.label: Two ancillas start in |0⟩, alongside the data qubit |ψ⟩
steps.sub: |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, the state to protect

steps.label: CNOT(qubit 1 → qubit 2), then CNOT(qubit 1 → qubit 3)
steps.sub: Two gates, entangling all three qubits together

steps.label: The joint state becomes α|000⟩ + β|111⟩
steps.sub: Genuinely entangled — not three independent copies of |ψ⟩

steps.label: No single qubit, alone, holds α and β
steps.sub: This is spreading, the move that gets around no-cloning

steps.label: Both |000⟩ and |111⟩ are +1 eigenstates of both
steps.sub: An error-free encoded state always measures '+1, no disagreement'

steps.label: Neither measurement reveals α or β
steps.sub: Both terms of the superposition agree on the outcome

eyebrow: The verified syndrome table, starting from |0⟩_L = |000⟩
code:
Error location   State    Syndrome (Z1Z2,Z2Z3)   Correction
None              000      00                      none needed
Qubit 1           100      10                      flip qubit 1
Qubit 2           010      11                      flip qubit 2
Qubit 3           001      01                      flip qubit 3
caption: Every one of these 4 cases decodes correctly, 100% of the time — the 2-bit syndrome alone tells you exactly which qubit to flip.

steps.label: A Z error changes relative phase, not any bit value
steps.sub: No disagreement shows up in Z1Z2 or Z2Z3

steps.label: The syndrome reads 00 — as if nothing happened
steps.sub: While the logical state has actually been corrupted

steps.label: This code corrects X errors only, perfectly
steps.sub: Protecting against Z errors needs a different, complementary code

subtitle: The exact mirror image, built in a rotated basis to catch what this code misses.
